children: The real estate sector saw most companies beating earnings estimates last week, but lagging on the revenue front, with only 60% of them showing an annual revenue growth.
Of the 10 companies that reported, eight firms (80%) exceeded FFO estimates, while one fell short and one was in line with market expectations. Notably, 7 firms (70%) posted Y/Y earnings growth.

Of the 10 companies, only 4 firms (40%) exceeded revenue expectations, while 6 of them fell below analyst estimates. Notably, only six firms (60%) reported year-over-year earnings growth, while one was flat and three reported an annual decline.
Let’s take a look at some real estate companies that reported earnings this week:

reported Q3 revenue of $1.62B, topping the $1.45B consensus, and an adjusted FFO per share of $1.12, beating the average analyst estimate of $1.10. Q3 same-store rental revenue growth slipped to 1.1% Y/Y vs. 1.2% Y/Y growth in Q2. The net lease REIT now expects full-year adjusted FFO per share at $4.45-$4.46

posted a Q3 revenue of $1.81B, beating the $1.66B consensus, and a real estate FFO per share of $3.37, exceeding the Visible Alpha estimate of $3.29. The company now expects 2026 real estate FFO per share of $13.30-$13.40 (midpoint $13.35) vs. the Visible Alpha consensus of $13.29.

delivered stronger-than-expected Q3 revenue of $1.99B as its growth businesses of data center, digital, and asset lifecycle management, together, grew more than 30% Y/Y. Q3 adjusted FFO per share of $1.53, beating the Visible Alpha consensus of $1.48. The company expects Q4 revenue of ~$2.03B, vs. the average analyst estimate of $2.05B.

title: Real Estate Earnings Scorecard: 40% firms beat revenue estimates, 60% post Y/Y growth
